question_text: What are extensive and intensive properties? Give examples.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Extensive properties
lines: Extensive properties depend on the amount
of matter present in the system.
steps.why: Doubling the sample doubles these values, so they measure the sample as a whole, not the substance itself.
common_mistakes: Giving only the definition. The examples carry part of the mark.
Listing density or temperature here — those do not change with amount.
steps.memory_tip: Extensive follows the extent of the sample: more matter, larger value.
steps.margin_note: Definition plus at least two examples.

steps.label: Intensive properties
lines: Intensive properties do not depend on the
amount of matter present in the system.

lines.text: Extensive: depends on amount. Intensive: does not.

steps.why: These values describe the substance and its condition, so a drop of water and a bucket of water at the same temperature share them.
common_mistakes: Writing heat capacity as intensive — heat capacity is extensive; SPECIFIC heat capacity (per gram) is intensive.
steps.memory_tip: Cut the sample in half: mass halves (extensive), temperature stays the same (intensive).
steps.margin_note: Heat capacity vs specific heat capacity is the pair the examiner watches.

insider_note: A three-star definition pair. The pair the examiner watches is heat capacity: plain heat capacity is extensive, specific heat capacity is intensive — one word changes the answer.
